html:
The Montgomery bus boycott was a protest in which Black residents of Montgomery, Alabama, refused to ride the city's segregated buses for 381 days, from December 1955 to December 1956.

It began after Rosa Parks, a seamstress and activist, was arrested on 1 December 1955 for refusing to give up her seat to a white man. Local leaders chose a young pastor, Martin Luther King Jr., to head the boycott. Tens of thousands walked or shared cars despite arrests and the bombing of King's house.

In Browder v. Gayle the courts ruled bus segregation unconstitutional, and the Supreme Court upheld the ruling. The boycott showed the power of mass nonviolent protest against the Jim Crow laws and led to the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
sum: The Montgomery bus boycott was a protest in which Black residents of Montgomery, Alabama, refused to ride the city's segregated buses for 381 days, from December 1955 to December 1956.
